cases.name: alternating_returns
cases.why: lag-1 ACF is exactly -1 by construction; lag 50 unavailable

cases.derivation: alternating a,b gives cov = -((a-b)/2)^2 = -var, so acf1 = -1
cases.name: two_valued_magnitudes
cases.why: |return| alternates ln2, ln4 so the abs ACF is -1 and conditioned

cases.name: zero_change_fraction
cases.why: 3 unchanged of 4 consecutive pairs, a ratio of small integers

cases.finding: The zero-variance guard fires ONLY for an exactly-representable constant. A series constant at an irrational value - |return| = ln2 in the alternating fixture - leaves a tiny positive float residue as its variance, so the guard misses and the ACF is decided by catastrophic cancellation. Real market months always have positive return variance, so neither path fires in the batch, but the guard is narrower than it looks.
cases.name: constant_price
cases.why: degenerate but defined: zero_change_frac is 1.0, not unavailable

cases.name: insufficient_length
cases.why: one return is below AutoCorr's n>=2 floor; all ACF lags None

cases.name: size_round_fraction
cases.why: 4 of 10 sizes carry at most two significant decimals

cases.name: size_dispersion
cases.why: two log bins exactly 30 apart give a dispersion of 1000

cases.name: size_histogram_empty
cases.why: no positive size, so dispersion is unavailable rather than 0 or 1
